newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech seeks FCC help on cable TV access.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech seeks FCC help on cable TV access.

text.p: Ameritech Corp's cable television division said Thursday it would petition the U.S. Federal Communications Commission to help it gain access to television programming.
Deborah Lenart, president of Ameritech New Media, said at the company's monthly media briefing that the company would file a petition on Friday.
She said the company would ask for a shorter time period to solve complaints about access to programming and for financial penalties for companies that violate the rules.

"We're starting to be a little bit constrained," Lenart said, adding that Ameritech is looking for the FCC to put some "teeth" into the rules. "As the market becomes more and more competitive, you are going to see more complaints."

The federal Cable Act of 1992 established rules to ensure full access to programming in a competitive cable TV market. While cable providers are required to broadcast local programming, they are also required to make their own programming available to other providers at fair rates.
Ameritech said it currently has one outstanding complaint, against CableVision Systems over its Sports Channel Ohio.

Ameritech chairman and chief executive Richard Notebaert said the complaint process typically lasts more than a year, and in some cases has gone on for more than 2-1/2 years. He said the company would ask for a 60-day process, and would be happy with 90 days.
Ameritech New Media is responsible for launching and marketing Ameritech's cable TV service, called Americast. Ameritech currently has franchise agreements in 37 areas, reaching 750,000 homes.
